title.narrative: Building a disaster resilient media sector in the Caribbean

description.narrative:
The Caribbean is a region subject to multiple natural hazards, some of which due to climate change are becoming more frequent and intense threats to small island developing states (SIDS). These hazards influence the social, economic and environmental well-being of SIDS and their ability to achieve sustainability and assure the well-being of their populations. Informed planning and decision-making based on quality information and science, coupled with ongoing monitoring, public engagement and interventions can moderate the impact of hazards thereby reducing losses and shortening recovery times.
Journalists and the media sector are key actors with important roles in the hazard information flow cycle: interpreting, disseminating, critiquing as well as mobilizing the public in the pre/during and post hazard phases. Through this programme we will position the media sector to positively moderate this relation, by empowering media professionals and institutions with the requisite knowledge, competencies and skills. Strengthening their institutional capacities through the development and implementation of hazard risk assessments, the development of operational and business continuity plans and networks that integrate new technologies and best in class practices, so as to increase the sector's resilience to hazards while strengthening their ability to provide timely, effective and engaging programming on hazard preparedness and response to the countries and audiences they serve.
